content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Faced with growing globalization, students realize that a deep understanding of traditional Chinese culture helps cultivate cultural confidence." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
content.topic: Traditional Chinese culture and cultural confidence

modelEssay.title: Traditional Chinese Culture and Cultural Confidence
modelEssay.content:
Faced with growing globalization, students realize that a deep understanding of traditional Chinese culture helps cultivate cultural confidence. As different civilizations meet and mix more closely than ever before, a firm grasp of one's own roots becomes not a barrier to openness but the very foundation of it.

On the one hand, traditional Chinese culture—from Confucian ethics to classical poetry and festivals—offers students a stable sense of identity. When they know where they come from, they can engage the wider world with self-respect rather than blind imitation. On the other hand, cultural confidence encourages students to share Chinese wisdom abroad. A student who can explain the meaning of the Spring Festival or the philosophy behind a Tang poem becomes a natural ambassador of his or her nation.

In conclusion, understanding our own heritage and embracing the world are not in conflict. The deeper students dig into traditional Chinese culture, the more confidently they can stand on the global stage. Therefore, we should treasure our cultural roots while keeping an open mind toward others.

structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：重申理解本国文化与拥抱世界并不矛盾，呼吁珍视文化根脉、保持开放心态。

transcript.text: Welcome to Business Matters.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 欢迎收听《商业要闻》。

transcript.text: Today we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 今天我们邀请到了职业发展顾问露西·威廉姆斯，来谈谈如何在职场上脱颖而出。

transcript.text: Hi Lucy.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你好，露西。

transcript.text: Many of us never seem to get promoted.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们中的很多人似乎一直得不到晋升。

transcript.text: Why is that and what can we do about it?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这是为什么呢？我们又能做些什么来改变这种状况？

transcript.text: One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人们常犯的一个错误是只和上司沟通。

transcript.text: It's important to expand your network and include your co-workers.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 拓展自己的人脉网络、把同事也纳入其中，这一点很重要。

transcript.text: But some of our co-workers are less senior to us.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但我们有些同事的职级比我们低。

transcript.text: Is it really necessary to connect with them?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 真的有必要和他们建立联系吗？

transcript.text: It's important not to underestimate your colleagues.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 重要的是不要低估你的同事。

transcript.text: Sometimes a job title might not clearly demonstrate the influence they may have.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 有时候，一个人的职位头衔并不能清楚地体现出他可能拥有的影响力。

transcript.text: Now many of us think that working hard creates a good impression, but this isn't always true is it?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们很多人都认为努力工作会给人留下好印象，但事实并非总是如此，对吧？

transcript.text: That's right.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没错。

transcript.text: We should avoid trying to take on too much work and constantly staying late just to show that you are committed.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们应该避免为了显示自己敬业而承揽过多工作、并且总是加班到很晚。

transcript.text: I see.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我明白了。

transcript.text: So setting expectations too high at the beginning can make us look bad if we don't maintain them.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 所以，如果一开始就把期望值定得太高，之后又达不到，反而会让我们显得很糟糕。

transcript.text: Yeah, it's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，最好确保你投入的是高质量的时间，而不仅仅是大量的时间。

transcript.text: And these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 而这些努力可以很容易地通过我们取得的成果体现出来。

transcript.text: What about helping others at work?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那在工作中帮助他人又如何呢？

transcript.text: Should you try and go beyond your normal responsibilities and offer to help people with their projects?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你应该超出自己的本职工作范围，主动去帮别人做他们的项目吗？

transcript.text: Extend your assistance to those who need it, but only as long as your own work will not go unattended.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 向需要帮助的人伸出援手，但前提是不能耽误你自己的工作。

transcript.text: If someone can benefit from your assistance or advice, help them out to gain their respect and trust.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如果有人能从你的帮助或建议中受益，就帮他一把，以此赢得他们的尊重和信任。

transcript.text: But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all, otherwise you'll appear arrogant.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但不言而喻，你不该表现得无所不知，否则会显得很自大。

transcript.text: Absolutely.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 完全正确。

transcript.text: Be humble and you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 保持谦逊，日后你会有大把的时间来展现你的才华。

transcript.text: I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我觉得我们首先得决定怎么分配这次演讲的任务。

transcript.text: From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 据我记得，这次演讲一共有五个部分，还不包括引言和结论。

transcript.text: That would mean altogether we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那就意味着我们俩总共需要分配七个部分。

transcript.text: So we have the abstract, background research, the project design, the results and the discussion portions.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以我们有摘要、背景研究、项目设计、结果和讨论这几个部分。

transcript.text: As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn't include it in the presentation.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 由于摘要部分只适用于文章，我们在演讲中就不必包含它了。

transcript.text: How would you suggest we dole out the rest?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 剩下的部分你觉得我们该怎么分配呢？

transcript.text: How do you feel about handling the background bit?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你来负责背景这一部分，觉得怎么样？

transcript.text: In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这样一来，我们俩都能讲到自己投入时间最多的那部分项目内容。

transcript.text: Hold on a minute.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 等一下。

transcript.text: You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你想让我这个做了大部分工作的人，再来承担大部分的演讲？

transcript.text: The background research which was so meticulous took more than a month.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那么细致的背景研究可花了我一个多月。

transcript.text: Okay, okay, I get it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 好啦好啦，我明白了。

transcript.text: Quit your moaning.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 别再抱怨了。

transcript.text: I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我很欣赏你在研究中一丝不苟的工作态度，但不喜欢每次我一提起它你就冷嘲热讽。

transcript.text: What do you think would be a fair arrangement?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你觉得怎样分配才算公平呢？

transcript.text: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts, before 1980 and afterward.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我觉得最好的安排是把研究分成两部分，1980年以前和1980年以后。

transcript.text: I will take the before portion and you would be assigned the after 1980, leaving the project and results.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我负责1980年以前的部分，你负责1980年以后的，这样就剩下项目和结果部分了。

transcript.text: I volunteer to describe the project, but as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我自愿来讲项目部分，不过既然我在结果部分的数据统计上有点吃力，那部分就交给你处理，怎么样？

transcript.text: That's agreeable to me.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我同意。

transcript.text: I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我提议讨论部分我们俩分段来讲，随后的问答环节也一起负责，这样就只剩引言和结论了。

transcript.text: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我来负责结论，让你负责引言。

transcript.text: This will make it so that we alternate presenting, so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这样我们就能轮流演讲，从而避免让听众觉得单调乏味。

transcript.text: Makeup can do more than just change your appearance.
transcript.translation: 化妆的作用不仅仅是改变你的外貌。

transcript.text: It can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse.
transcript.translation: 它还能改变别人对你的看法，或好或坏。

transcript.text: According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious, positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.
transcript.translation: 根据苏格兰斯特灵大学的一项新研究，尽管男性和女性都认为化妆的女性地位更高，但男性会把化妆与令人尊敬的正面品质联系在一起，而女性则把化妆的其他女性视为强势、构成潜在威胁的存在。

transcript.text: The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive.
transcript.translation: 研究显示，男性和女性都认为化了妆的面孔更具吸引力。

transcript.text: But only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.
transcript.translation: 但只有女性认为化了妆的面孔更强势，而只有男性认为化了妆的面孔更受尊敬。

transcript.text: A follow-up study investigated the root cause behind these differences in perception, and found that female on female jealousy seemed to be the main cause for the differences in perception.
transcript.translation: 一项后续研究调查了这些认知差异背后的根本原因，发现女性之间的嫉妒似乎是造成这些认知差异的主要原因。

transcript.text: Women rating women with makeup said they would be more jealous of them, and thought they would be more attractive to men than their non-makeup wearing counterparts.
transcript.translation: 对化妆女性进行评价的女性表示，她们会更嫉妒这些人，并认为她们比不化妆的女性对男性更有吸引力。

transcript.text: Cosmetic products are good for more than just giving you a pretty face.
transcript.translation: 化妆品的好处不仅仅是让你拥有一张漂亮的脸。

transcript.text: It can be particularly useful for women to understand how wearing makeup alters others' perceptions of them in situations where they are trying to gain others' trust and admiration.
transcript.translation: 在女性试图赢得他人信任和赞赏的场合，了解化妆会如何改变别人对自己的看法，可能会格外有用。

transcript.text: At a job interview, knowing whether the hiring committee will consist of men or women might influence a female candidate's decision about wearing makeup.
transcript.translation: 在求职面试中，了解招聘委员会是由男性还是女性组成，可能会影响一位女性求职者是否化妆的决定。

transcript.text: Whether the interviewers will view her as attractive, dominant and prestigious can affect the interviewer's actions and perhaps the outcome of the interview itself.
transcript.translation: 面试官是否会认为她有吸引力、强势且值得尊敬，可能会影响面试官的行为，甚至可能影响面试本身的结果。

transcript.text: You may have seen advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever.
transcript.translation: 你也许见过一些广告，大肆宣扬某些改变习惯的方法完全不需要任何意志力。

transcript.text: But can you really change a bad habit or create a good one without willpower?
transcript.translation: 但没有意志力，你真的能改掉一个坏习惯或养成一个好习惯吗？

transcript.text: To answer this question we first have to ask, what is willpower?
transcript.translation: 要回答这个问题，我们首先得问：什么是意志力？

transcript.text: Most people sadly think of it only as the ability to clench their teeth and resist attractive temptations.
transcript.translation: 遗憾的是，大多数人只把它看作咬紧牙关、抵挡诱人诱惑的能力。

transcript.text: In this view, willpower means self-denial and no fun.
transcript.translation: 按这种看法，意志力就意味着克己自律、毫无乐趣。

transcript.text: No wonder people hope to make changes without it.
transcript.translation: 难怪人们都希望不靠意志力就能做出改变。

transcript.text: I define willpower as using only the thought of your motivators to control your actions.
transcript.translation: 我对意志力的定义是：仅凭对自身动力的念想来控制自己的行为。

transcript.text: Let's say your motivators are prevent diabetes and reach a healthy weight.
transcript.translation: 假设你的动力是预防糖尿病和达到健康体重。

transcript.text: So if you are at the all-you-can-eat buffet, you think about your motivator, avoid diabetes through weight loss, and you take small portions and avoid the dessert table.
transcript.translation: 所以如果你身处自助餐厅，你就想想自己的动力——通过减重来预防糖尿病，于是你只取少量食物，并避开甜点区。

transcript.text: So amazingly enough, willpower begins with a thought, a bright idea, some way to improve your life or contribute to others.
transcript.translation: 所以奇妙的是，意志力始于一个念头、一个好主意，某种能改善你的生活或惠及他人的方式。

transcript.text: This bright idea is your motivator.
transcript.translation: 这个好主意就是你的动力。

transcript.text: Dr. Walter Mischel, an expert on willpower skills, uses the expressive term, a burning goal.
transcript.translation: 意志力技巧专家沃尔特·米歇尔博士用了一个生动的说法，叫做“炽热的目标”。

transcript.text: Whether you call it a motivator, a burning goal, or a bright idea, this idea is the force behind your willpower.
transcript.translation: 无论你把它称作动力、炽热的目标还是好主意，这个念头都是你意志力背后的力量。

transcript.text: What sort of bright ideas motivators make for effective willpower?
transcript.translation: 什么样的好主意或动力才能造就有效的意志力呢？

transcript.text: In fact, any goal that you value strongly counts.
transcript.translation: 事实上，任何你极为看重的目标都算数。

transcript.text: The list may include good health, self-respect, a better future for your family, personal mission, and being a role model for your child.
transcript.translation: 这些目标可能包括身体健康、自尊、给家人更美好的未来、个人使命，以及成为孩子的榜样。

transcript.text: All these can certainly drive a positive change.
transcript.translation: 所有这些都确实能推动一种积极的改变。

transcript.text: For many pregnant women, understanding what seafood is safe and healthy and what should be avoided because of mercury concerns comes with a lot of worrying.
transcript.translation: 对许多孕妇来说，弄清楚哪些海鲜安全又健康、哪些因汞含量问题应当避免，总是伴随着诸多担忧。

transcript.text: In part, that's because the federal government's advice on the matter, first issued in 2004, has long been criticized as vague.
transcript.translation: 这在一定程度上是因为联邦政府就此事发布的建议（最初于2004年颁布）长期以来一直被批评为含糊不清。

transcript.text: That guidance has included advice on how much seafood to eat and which species pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid over concerns about mercury contamination.
transcript.translation: 该指南包含了关于该吃多少海鲜、以及出于对汞污染的担忧孕妇和哺乳期妇女应避免哪些鱼类的建议。

transcript.text: But critics say the government advisory has done more harm than good, scaring many pregnant and breastfeeding women away from eating seafood altogether.
transcript.translation: 但批评者称，政府的这份建议弊大于利，把许多孕妇和哺乳期妇女吓得完全不敢吃海鲜了。

transcript.text: The problem is real.
transcript.translation: 这个问题确实存在。

transcript.text: According to a spokesman for the Food and Drug Administration, or FDA for short, the agency analyzed fish consumption data from more than 1,000 pregnant women in the U.S. and found that 21% of them ate no fish whatsoever in the previous month.
transcript.translation: 据美国食品药品监督管理局（简称FDA）的一位发言人称，该机构分析了美国1000多名孕妇的鱼类食用数据，发现其中21%的人在过去一个月里完全没有吃鱼。

transcript.text: And those who did eat fish consumed far less than recommended by the dietary guidelines.
transcript.translation: 而那些确实吃鱼的人，摄入量也远低于膳食指南的推荐值。

transcript.text: Some 50% ate less than 2 ounces a week and 75% ate less than 4 ounces.
transcript.translation: 约有50%的人每周吃鱼不足2盎司，75%的人每周吃鱼不足4盎司。

transcript.text: This week, the FDA issued an update to the advice, listing more than 60 species in a chart that ranks fish as a best choice, good choice, and choices to avoid.
transcript.translation: 本周，FDA发布了该建议的更新版，在一张图表中列出了60多种鱼类，把它们分为最佳选择、良好选择和应避免的选择。

transcript.text: The goal is to make it easier for mothers to be to feel confident about the type of seafood they include in their diets.
transcript.translation: 其目的是让准妈妈们更容易对自己饮食中所选的海鲜种类感到放心。

transcript.text: The new advice recommends consumers choose a variety of fish to eat, and it comes with an easy to understand illustration of what an appropriate portion size should be.
transcript.translation: 新建议推荐消费者选择多种鱼类食用，并配有一张通俗易懂的图示，说明合适的份量应该是多少。

transcript.text: Four ounces for an adult and two ounces for children aged 4 to 7.
transcript.translation: 成人4盎司，4至7岁的儿童2盎司。

transcript.text: And while expectant mothers have long been warned to stay away from shark and four other particular types of fish from the Gulf of Mexico, now there are three new species on the list of what to avoid.
transcript.translation: 虽然一直以来准妈妈们都被告诫要远离鲨鱼以及来自墨西哥湾的另外四种特定鱼类，如今应避免的清单上又新增了三个鱼种。

transcript.text: But not everyone is thrilled with the new advice.
transcript.translation: 但并非所有人都对这份新建议感到满意。

transcript.text: Critics say the new advice doesn't always agree with the agency's own scientific findings.
transcript.translation: 批评者称，这份新建议并不总是与该机构自己的科学发现相一致。

transcript.text: While mercury is of great concern when people are talking about pregnant women and seafood, it's not the only factor contributing to anxiety.
transcript.translation: 在人们谈论孕妇与海鲜时，汞固然备受关注，但它并不是引发焦虑的唯一因素。

transcript.text: The FDA maintains that its final consumption recommendations were based on thorough scientific analysis.
transcript.translation: FDA坚称，其最终的食用建议是基于全面的科学分析得出的。

transcript.text: Agency spokesman Kassell says the FDA believes the recommendations will increase confidence, not uncertainty.
transcript.translation: 该机构发言人卡塞尔表示，FDA相信这些建议会增强人们的信心，而非带来更多的不确定性。

transcript.text: But critics disagree.
transcript.translation: 但批评者并不认同。

transcript.text: They think the FDA's advice is not based on the evidence in its own detailed report, and so it confuses everyone.
transcript.translation: 他们认为FDA的建议并非基于其自身详尽报告中的证据，因此让大家都感到困惑。

transcript.text: I know you're busy with work, but you also need to take some time off to recharge those batteries.
transcript.translation: 我知道你工作很忙，但你也需要抽点时间休息一下，给自己充充电。

transcript.text: So, should you plan one big vacation for the year?
transcript.translation: 那么，你应该为这一年安排一次大的假期吗？

transcript.text: Or should you take multiple short vacations throughout?
transcript.translation: 还是应该全年分几次休短假？

transcript.text: Quantity can sometimes beat quality.
transcript.translation: 数量有时候能胜过质量。

transcript.text: First and foremost, regardless of how you use your vacation days, you need to be using them, and soon.
transcript.translation: 首先，最重要的是，无论你怎么使用你的假期，你都得把它们用起来，而且要尽快。

transcript.text: The longer you put off your time off, the worse you're making things for yourself.
transcript.translation: 你越是拖着不休假，对自己就越不利。

transcript.text: One nine-year-long study published in psychosomatic medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease.
transcript.translation: 一项发表在《身心医学》上、历时九年的研究表明，一年连一次假都不休，可能会增加你因心脏病而死亡的风险。

transcript.text: So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself.
transcript.translation: 所以，你不仅是在扼杀自己的快乐，还可能是在葬送自己的生命。

transcript.text: Give yourself a break, folks.
transcript.translation: 各位，给自己放个假吧。

transcript.text: When you should take those breaks, however, depends on a few factors.
transcript.translation: 不过，你该在什么时候休假，取决于几个因素。

transcript.text: How many days you have available to use, what activities bring you joy, whether you have a family or not, and other variables come into play.
transcript.translation: 你有多少天假可以用、什么活动能给你带来快乐、你有没有家庭，以及其他各种因素都会起作用。

transcript.text: Because of that, there's no perfect formula that works for everyone, but there are still a few things everyone can try to shoot for.
transcript.translation: 正因如此，没有一个适用于所有人的完美公式，但仍有几点是每个人都可以努力争取的。

transcript.text: We know that, in terms of maximizing relaxation, you should aim for vacations that range somewhere between seven and eleven days long.
transcript.translation: 我们知道，就最大限度地放松而言，你应当把假期安排在七到十一天之间。

transcript.text: That gives you enough time to let go of your stress at work, completely loosen up, and achieve full-on calm.
transcript.translation: 这能给你足够的时间来释放工作压力、彻底放松下来，并进入完全平静的状态。

transcript.text: That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once.
transcript.translation: 上面提到的那项研究还建议你把假期均匀地分开安排，而不要一次性把所有假都用完。

transcript.text: Eight days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets ten days of vacation a year, but if you frame them with weekends, you can manage two evenly spaced eight-day vacations a year.
transcript.translation: 对于一年只有十天假的人来说，八天听起来可能很多，但如果你把它们和周末拼在一起，一年就能安排两次间隔均匀的八天假期。

transcript.text: If you have fourteen days of paid leave, that's almost three separate eight-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds.
transcript.translation: 如果你有十四天带薪假，那差不多就是三次各八天的独立假期，你可以用它们把一年分成三段。

transcript.text: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency.
transcript.translation: 尽管把所有假都用来休一个漫长的暑假很诱人，但你的总体目标应当是在假期长度、快乐感和频率之间取得完美的平衡。

transcript.text: Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to.
transcript.translation: 休假频率很重要，因为全年安排多次假期意味着你总有值得期待的事情。

transcript.text: Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tends to make us happier.
transcript.translation: 做计划以及随之而来的期待，往往会让我们更快乐。

transcript.text: If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.
transcript.translation: 如果你每年只休一次长假，兴奋感积累得会慢得多，而且假期显得如此遥远，反而可能让人产生绝望的情绪。

transcript.text: Autonomous cars that can take over from drivers if they are tired or distracted are being developed in Sweden.
transcript.translation: 瑞典正在研发能在驾驶员疲劳或分神时接管车辆的自动驾驶汽车。

transcript.text: Researchers working as part of the European Union's 77 billion euro research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious, or tired.
transcript.translation: 作为欧盟770亿欧元研究项目一部分的研究人员，正在研发基于传感器的系统，用来监测驾驶员是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。

transcript.text: If a driver is not in a fit state to be on the road, the car automatically takes control of the wheel to prevent accidents.
transcript.translation: 如果驾驶员的状态不适合上路，汽车会自动接管方向盘以防止事故发生。

transcript.text: Dr. Anna Anund from the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who is leading the project, said a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is.
transcript.translation: 领导该项目的瑞典国家道路与交通研究所的安娜·阿农德博士表示，驾驶员的状态可以通过多种传感器来测量，包括心率监测器和追踪驾驶员视线方向的眼动传感器。

transcript.text: She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.
transcript.translation: 她说，目标是要真正确保从驾驶员到车辆的控制权交接以安全的方式完成，这样我们就能把驾驶员的状态考虑进去，从而不会把控制权交给正承受疲劳、压力、焦虑等困扰的驾驶员。

transcript.text: According to data from the European Commission, Sweden has the safest roads in the EU, with the UK a close second.
transcript.translation: 根据欧盟委员会的数据，瑞典拥有欧盟内最安全的道路，英国紧随其后位居第二。

transcript.text: However, the number of road accidents in both has largely leveled out since 2010.
transcript.translation: 然而，自2010年以来，两国的交通事故数量基本上都趋于平稳。

transcript.text: Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen.
transcript.translation: 据认为，在整个欧盟范围内多达五分之一的交通事故是由驾驶员疲劳造成的，不过一天中某些时段发生的事故会更多。

transcript.text: At 6am, for example, drivers are said to be 20 times more likely to have an accident than at 10am.
transcript.translation: 比如说，据称在凌晨6点，驾驶员发生事故的可能性是上午10点的20倍。

transcript.text: While most experts agree driverless technology should help bring down accident numbers in the long term, some have questioned whether it is safe.
transcript.translation: 尽管大多数专家都认同无人驾驶技术从长远看应有助于减少事故数量，但也有人质疑它是否安全。

transcript.text: The researchers have said the technology they are developing is seeking to bridge the gap between level 3 on the autonomy scale, in which drivers have to be ready to take control of the car at any point, and level 4, in which driving is automated.
transcript.translation: 研究人员表示，他们正在研发的技术旨在弥合自动驾驶等级中三级与四级之间的差距：三级要求驾驶员随时准备接管车辆，而四级则实现驾驶自动化。

transcript.text: Daniel Ruiz, the chief executive of the UK's Connected and Autonomous Vehicle Program, Meridian, said, There is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a level 3 car completely safe.
transcript.translation: 英国网联与自动驾驶汽车项目Meridian的首席执行官丹尼尔·鲁伊斯说：“关于如何才能让三级汽车做到完全安全，目前存在着激烈的争论。”

transcript.text: Despite advances in technology, we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment.
transcript.translation: 尽管技术不断进步，我们在转变公众情绪方面仍有一段路要走。

transcript.text: With an increase in attention grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.
transcript.translation: 近来引人关注的事故有所增多，如今驾驶员们认为自动驾驶汽车不如以往那样安全了。

questionGroups.title: Meet the 'digital nomads' who travel the world in search of fast Wi-Fi

material.title: Meet the 'digital nomads' who travel the world in search of fast Wi-Fi

paragraphs.text: For those "citizens of the world", the office can be anything from a beach hut in Brisbane to a Starbucks in Seattle, thanks to the growing prevalence of remote-based work. But roaming the globe from café to café is not without its challenges.
paragraphs.translation: 对于那些"世界公民"来说，随着远程办公日益普及，办公室可以是布里斯班的一间海滨小屋，也可以是西雅图的一家星巴克。但从一家咖啡馆漫游到另一家咖啡馆、周游世界，也并非没有挑战。

paragraphs.text: When the average traveller lands in a city like Bangkok, Berlin, or Buenos Aires, their first step might be to drop their bags at their hotel and to log on to TripAdvisor to find out the hours of a popular tourist attraction or the best rooftop bar for happy hour.
paragraphs.translation: 当普通旅行者抵达曼谷、柏林或布宜诺斯艾利斯这样的城市时，他们的第一步也许是把行李放到酒店，然后登录 TripAdvisor，查一查热门景点的开放时间或欢乐时光最棒的屋顶酒吧。

paragraphs.text: But people like Pieter Levels are not your average traveller. A Dutch website developer, Levels has been living and working nomadically (像游牧民那样) in places like Singapore, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Manila for two years. With just a carry-on backpack, he chooses his location at will, based on a variety of factors—Wi-Fi speed, average temperature, exotic food and cost of living—that have little bearing on the work he actually does.
paragraphs.translation: 但像 Pieter Levels 这样的人并不是普通旅行者。作为一名荷兰网站开发者，Levels 两年来一直像游牧民那样在新加坡、香港、东京和马尼拉等地生活和工作。他只带一个随身背包，随心所欲地选择所在地，依据的是 Wi-Fi 速度、平均气温、异域美食和生活成本等各种因素——而这些因素与他实际所做的工作几乎毫无关系。

paragraphs.text: Somewhere in his nomadic journey, Levels noticed that there was a growing need to create an online infrastructure for people like himself. That's when he created #nomads, a membership-based chat system which runs on the team communication platform known as Slack. The channel allows users to ask people in their current city the types of practical questions that a tourist would unlikely need to ask.
paragraphs.translation: 在他游牧旅程的某个阶段，Levels 注意到，为像他这样的人建立一个在线基础设施的需求正在增长。于是他创建了 #nomads，这是一个基于会员制的聊天系统，运行在名为 Slack 的团队沟通平台上。该频道允许用户向所在城市的其他人提出各种实际问题，而这些问题通常是游客不太需要问的。

paragraphs.text: Members of the geographically dispersed subculture that Levels is a part of call themselves "digital nomads". They are borderless, mostly self-employed remote workers who interact with cities in a way that's entirely different from a tourist, but still doesn't quite reach the status of resident. A relatively new phenomenon, there are no hard statistics on the prevalence of digital nomads or location independent workers. But thanks to the growing prevalence of freelance (自由职业的) livelihoods, a global sharing economy and numerous digital tools, the number of people who are able to live this life is growing quickly. And in a rapidly urbanising world, where a major city in Asia increasingly offers the same comforts as one in Europe, many people are reaching the realisation they don't need to stay in one place.
paragraphs.translation: Levels 所属的这一地理上分散的亚文化群体成员自称为"数字游民"。他们没有边界，大多是自雇的远程工作者，与城市互动的方式和游客完全不同，但又还没有达到居民的身份。作为一个相对较新的现象，关于数字游民或不受地点限制的工作者到底有多普遍，并没有确切的统计数据。但得益于自由职业生活方式的日益普及、全球共享经济以及众多数字工具，能够过上这种生活的人数正在迅速增长。而在一个快速城市化的世界里，亚洲的大城市越来越能提供与欧洲城市同样的舒适条件，许多人开始意识到，他们不必固守一地。

paragraphs.text: So how does a nomad differ from a tourist or resident? In many ways, Levels says, you can think of a digital nomad like a "short-term independent expat (移居国外的人)". Unlike a resident expat, they don't work for a large multinational company in an air conditioned office building and they generally enter a country on a tourist visa, simply renewing or moving on when it expires. But unlike a tourist, they don't arrive in a foreign city without any responsibilities. Travel isn't necessarily required for them to do their jobs, but neither is staying in one place.
paragraphs.translation: 那么游民与游客或居民有何不同？Levels 说，在很多方面，你可以把数字游民想象成"短期的独立侨民"。与定居的侨民不同，他们不为空调办公楼里的大型跨国公司工作，通常持旅游签证入境，签证到期时只是续签或转往他处。但与游客不同，他们抵达异国城市时并非毫无责任在身。旅行对他们完成工作而言并非必需，但固守一地同样也不是。

paragraphs.text: Janet Brent is an independent ebook designer. She says many people she knows assume she travels for work, but in reality her international destinations are largely up to her, and driven by cost. "Contrary to what some people might think, I don't get paid to travel—I simply choose the lifestyle. Rather than rent in one given city, I choose to travel and do short-term, temporary stays around the world, and my travel decisions are literally based on what makes the most sense financially for me," Brent said. "It's completely different from vacationing—you really sink into the city life and get your feet wet in the communities."
paragraphs.translation: Janet Brent 是一名独立电子书设计师。她说，许多认识她的人以为她是为工作而旅行，但实际上她的国际目的地基本由自己决定，并受成本驱动。"与一些人的想法相反，我不是靠旅行赚钱——我只是选择了这种生活方式。与其在某一座城市租房，我选择周游世界、进行短期临时停留，我的旅行决定完全基于对我而言在经济上最划算的选择，" Brent 说。"这和度假完全不同——你真正沉浸到城市生活中，融入当地社区。"

paragraphs.text: Bryce Adams is another such nomad. He works as a developer for a South African company WooThemes, which has a workforce that's more than 80% remote-based. Though Adams frequently posts pictures on Instagram of his enviable cooking adventures from Seoul to Bangkok, he says nomad life in foreign cities has its downsides, including finding adequate Wi-Fi for the bandwidth-hungry work his livelihood depends on. Contrary to the perception that he works under a mango tree in a tropical haven, Adams says the reality of this life means that he often ends up staying in more western style places in globalised cities—ones that are sure to have air conditioning and a decent connection—rather than exotic beachfront cafés.
paragraphs.translation: Bryce Adams 是另一位这样的游民。他为南非公司 WooThemes 担任开发者，该公司超过80%的员工都是远程办公。尽管 Adams 经常在 Instagram 上发布他从首尔到曼谷令人羡慕的烹饪冒险照片，他说在异国城市的游民生活也有其不利之处，包括为他赖以谋生的高带宽工作寻找足够好的 Wi-Fi。与人们以为他在热带天堂的芒果树下工作的印象相反，Adams 说这种生活的现实是，他常常最终待在全球化城市里更西式的场所——那些一定有空调和不错网络的地方——而不是异域的海滨咖啡馆。

paragraphs.text: "A fellow nomad posted quite a funny but honest message on Twitter a few days ago that stuck with me: 'It's funny that digital nomads spend 16 hours to fly to the other side of the world to sit in Starbucks,' and it's completely true," Adams said. "When you're a digital nomad, you don't actually have as much freedom as most people think you do. We have deadlines, we all have people relying on us and a mouth (or two) that needs to be fed. It's nice to be able to work anywhere in the world but it's not without its challenges."
paragraphs.translation: "几天前，一位游民同伴在 Twitter 上发了一条相当好笑但真实的消息，让我印象深刻：'有趣的是，数字游民花16个小时飞到地球另一端，就为了坐在星巴克里，'而这完全是真的，" Adams 说。"当你成为数字游民，你实际上并没有大多数人以为的那么自由。我们有截止期限，我们都有依赖我们的人，还有一张（甚至两张）要养活的嘴。能在世界任何地方工作固然很好，但也并非没有挑战。"

paragraphs.text: But these challenges can often provide an opportunity for nomads to see a side of a city they may not have if they were staying in a luxury hotel for a long weekend. However inconvenient, a trip to a local doctor, immigration office or laundry—or a conflict with a local Airbnb host (the accommodation style of choice for most nomads)—can be far more culturally instructive than a trip to the national museum. And because nomads often have to stay where the strongest internet connection is, they tend to spend more time in developing cities compared to the average tourist, who often flees to more touristy destinations soon after landing at the airport.
paragraphs.translation: 但这些挑战往往能给游民一个机会，让他们看到一座城市中若只是在豪华酒店度过一个长周末就无缘得见的一面。无论多么不便，去看当地医生、办理移民手续或洗衣，或与当地 Airbnb 房东（大多数游民首选的住宿方式）发生一点摩擦——都可能比参观国家博物馆更具文化启发意义。而且由于游民往往必须待在网络连接最强的地方，与普通游客相比，他们在发展中城市待的时间更多；而普通游客常常一落地就奔向更具旅游气息的目的地。

paragraphs.text: The nomad life is, by all accounts, one built out of privilege. You not only need a relatively powerful passport that makes tourist visas easy to attain, but also a knowledge economy job and access to the technology and devices that make remote working possible. But nomads like Adams say that while they are aware of this privilege, they believe living this way elevates what they're able to offer, by giving them a broader perspective on what they're building, writing, or designing and expanding their world view.
paragraphs.translation: 无论从哪个角度看，游民生活都是一种建立在特权之上的生活。你不仅需要一本相对'强大'、便于获取旅游签证的护照，还需要一份知识经济领域的工作，以及能让远程办公成为可能的技术和设备。但像 Adams 这样的游民说，尽管他们意识到这种特权，他们相信这样的生活方式提升了他们所能贡献的价值——它让他们对自己所构建、所写作或所设计的东西有了更广阔的视角，并拓展了他们的世界观。

paragraphs.text: "Being able to travel and get around makes it easy to stay inspired," he added. "I truly believe that it makes me a more sensible human being, as I tend to see and appreciate the creative solutions people come up with in other parts of the world, even though many tend to have far more constraints than we have at home."
paragraphs.translation: "能够旅行、四处走动让人很容易保持灵感，" 他补充道。"我真心相信这让我成为一个更明理的人，因为我往往能看到并欣赏世界其他地方的人们想出的创造性解决方案，尽管其中许多人面临的限制远比我们在国内多得多。"

paragraphs.text: So when you're constantly on the road and don't own any property or have a fixed address, which city do you call home? It's no surprise that many nomads are dual citizens or "third culture kids," who have grown up with a notion of identity that's not tied to nationalism or staying in one place. Levels says that the nomad life has not only changed his notions of citizenship, but the people he chooses to spend time with as well. "Saying you're a 'citizen of the world' is a super cliché, right? But it's becoming quite true," Levels said. "This global awareness has been the reason I started Nomad List and it's affected who my friends are. It's normal to have dinner now and sit with a Korean girl, a British-Singaporean guy, a Mexican girl and a Nigerian guy. As much as that sounds like a politically correct TV advertisement, it's great that that's the time we're in now."
paragraphs.translation: 那么，当你常年在路上、不拥有任何房产、也没有固定住址时，你会把哪座城市称作家？难怪许多游民是双重国籍者或"第三文化孩子"，他们成长过程中形成的身份认同观念并不与民族主义或固守一地绑定。Levels 说，游民生活不仅改变了他关于公民身份的观念，也改变了他选择与之相处的人。"说自己是'世界公民'是个超级老套的说法，对吧？但它正在变得相当真实，" Levels 说。"这种全球意识正是我创办 Nomad List 的原因，它也影响了我的朋友是谁。如今，晚餐时和一个韩国女孩、一个英国裔新加坡小伙、一个墨西哥女孩以及一个尼日利亚小伙同桌，是再正常不过的事。尽管这听起来像一则政治正确的电视广告，但我们能身处这样的时代，实在是件好事。"

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: Pieter Levels created a chat system to satisfy the need of digital nomads for information tourists normally don't seek.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 D。段落 D 提到 Levels 创建了 #nomads 聊天系统，允许用户提出'a tourist would unlikely need to ask'的实际问题，与陈述中'information tourists normally don't seek'吻合。

questions.statementText: It is said that digital nomads do not enjoy as much freedom as most people suppose.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 I。段落 I 中 Adams 说'you don't actually have as much freedom as most people think you do'，与陈述中'do not enjoy as much freedom as most people suppose'一致。

questions.statementText: Different from tourists, digital nomads travel to foreign places with work to do.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 F。段落 F 指出'unlike a tourist, they don't arrive in a foreign city without any responsibilities'，即游民与游客不同、带着工作/责任而来，与陈述吻合。

questions.statementText: Digital nomads believe their lifestyle enables them to broaden their vision and do a better job.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 K。段落 K 提到这种生活方式'elevates what they're able to offer'并'expanding their world view'，即拓宽视野、提升工作价值，与陈述一致。

questions.statementText: The first thing a typical traveller possibly does after arriving at a city is search for information online about its popular tourist attractions.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 B。段落 B 描述普通旅行者抵达城市后'log on to TripAdvisor to find out the hours of a popular tourist attraction'，与陈述中'search for information online about its popular tourist attractions'吻合。

questions.statementText: One digital nomad thinks their life in foreign cities has its disadvantages.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 H。段落 H 中 Adams 说'nomad life in foreign cities has its downsides'，downsides 对应 disadvantages，与陈述一致。

questions.statementText: Travelling around helps to keep digital nomads inspired.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 L。段落 L 中'Being able to travel and get around makes it easy to stay inspired'与陈述几乎逐词对应。

questions.statementText: The number of self-employed remote workers living a digital nomad's life is fast increasing.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 E。段落 E 说明数字游民多为'self-employed remote workers'，且'the number of people who are able to live this life is growing quickly'，与陈述一致。

questions.statementText: Pieter Levels says his life as a nomad has transformed not only his idea of citizenship, but his choice of companions.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 M。段落 M 中 Levels 说游民生活'has not only changed his notions of citizenship, but the people he chooses to spend time with as well'，与陈述吻合。

questions.statementText: Interactions with local people and institutions provide nomads with far more cultural information than a visit to the national museum.
questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落 J。段落 J 指出去看当地医生、办移民手续或与 Airbnb 房东打交道'can be far more culturally instructive than a trip to the national museum'，与陈述一致。

questionGroups.title: Passage 1

paragraphs.text: Children's use of social media is a problem. That doesn't mean it should be stopped. While younger children should not be on platforms where 13 is the minimum age, it is neither practical nor desirable to imagine a world in which teenagers are prevented from accessing the platforms and messaging systems that the adults around them use to organise their lives.
paragraphs.translation: 儿童使用社交媒体是个问题，但这并不意味着应当禁止。虽然年龄更小的孩子不应出现在最低年龄要求为13岁的平台上，但设想一个青少年被禁止使用其周围成年人用来安排生活的各种平台和通讯系统的世界，既不现实也不可取。

paragraphs.text: But the pleasure and stimulation that people of all ages find on their screens and smartphones must not blind us to the harm that spending time in this way can cause. The finding that the alarmingly high rate of depression in British teenage girls is closely correlated to time spent on social media is extremely concerning. Research found that two in five girls are on social media for at least three hours a day—with half as many boys engaged to the same extent. More than a third of depressed girls have experienced online harassment. About half of affected girls suffered disrupted sleep, compared with 20% of depressed boys.
paragraphs.translation: 但各年龄段的人在屏幕和智能手机上获得的愉悦和刺激，绝不能使我们对这种消磨时间方式可能造成的危害视而不见。研究发现，英国少女中令人担忧的高抑郁率与在社交媒体上花费的时间密切相关，这一发现极其令人忧虑。研究发现，五分之二的女孩每天至少在社交媒体上花三个小时——达到同样程度的男孩数量只有女孩的一半。超过三分之一的抑郁女孩曾遭遇网络骚扰。约有一半受影响的女孩出现睡眠紊乱，而抑郁男孩中这一比例为20%。

paragraphs.text: Although the research does not prove that social media causes depression, the importance of the finding that there is a connection should not be underestimated. Schools have done important work in communicating key messages about the risks of online abuse. But when it comes to broader questions about "screen time", many professionals as well as parents are confused and uncertain.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管这项研究并未证明社交媒体导致抑郁，但对于两者之间存在关联这一发现的重要性，不应被低估。学校在传达有关网络欺凌风险的关键信息方面做了重要工作。但一旦涉及关于"屏幕时间"的更宽泛的问题，许多专业人士和家长都感到困惑和不确定。

paragraphs.text: The health secretary, Matt Hancock, wants official guidelines on time and age limits. This idea has the virtue of simplicity, though some experts question its effects and call for a greater degree of differentiation, arguing that time online by itself is not a bad thing and it all depends on what you are doing. Also due this year is information commissioner Elizabeth Denham's Age Appropriate Design Code, covering the use of children's personal data. Both initiatives are welcome. But the government is playing catch-up. Statutory regulation of the digital media giants is long overdue. The failure to protect children from data harvesting and targeted advertising thus far is as shocking as the lack of concern shown by the companies themselves with regard to children's psychological health.
paragraphs.translation: 卫生大臣 Matt Hancock 希望出台关于时间和年龄限制的官方指导方针。这一想法的优点在于简单，尽管一些专家质疑其效果，并呼吁进行更大程度的区分，认为上网时间本身并非坏事，一切取决于你在做什么。同样将在今年出台的还有信息专员 Elizabeth Denham 的《适龄设计准则》，涉及儿童个人数据的使用。这两项举措都值得欢迎。但政府是在追赶补课。对数字媒体巨头进行法定监管早就应该实施了。迄今未能保护儿童免受数据收割和定向广告之害，其令人震惊的程度，不亚于这些公司自身对儿童心理健康所表现出的漠不关心。

paragraphs.text: Of course, social media companies are not the source of all our ills, and can offer a too-easy target for politicians keen to divert attention from inadequately resourced schools and health services. There are other reasons for the rising incidence of depression in young people, with increasing pressure to succeed in education and in life more broadly—to be famous, beautiful, rich—often cited as a source of unhappiness or anxiety which can, if aggravated by other factors, and not managed, tip into ill health. Safeguarding means more than the avoidance of physical threat.
paragraphs.translation: 当然，社交媒体公司并非我们所有弊病的根源，对那些急于转移人们对资源不足的学校和医疗服务的注意力的政客而言，它们可能是一个过于轻易的靶子。年轻人抑郁发病率上升还有其他原因，在教育以及更广泛的人生中取得成功——出名、漂亮、富有——所带来的日益增大的压力，常被认为是不快乐或焦虑的来源；如果被其他因素加剧且得不到疏导，这种焦虑可能演变为疾病。保护孩子，意味着的远不止是避免身体上的威胁。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What does the author believe regarding social media?

options.label: A
options.text: To stop children using it is unrealistic and inadvisable.

options.label: B
options.text: It helps both adults and children to organise their lives.

options.label: C
options.text: It poses problems to both parents and children.

options.label: D
options.text: A world without it is really hard to imagine.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第一段指出儿童使用社交媒体是问题'但并不意味着应当禁止'，并称设想一个青少年被禁止使用相关平台的世界'既不现实也不可取（neither practical nor desirable）'，与 A（阻止儿童使用既不现实也不可取）一致。
questions.keySentence: it is neither practical nor desirable to imagine a world in which teenagers are prevented from accessing the platforms...

wrongOptions.B: 'organise their lives'指成年人用平台安排生活，并非说社交媒体帮助成人和儿童，理解偏差。
wrongOptions.C: 文中未强调对'父母和儿童'双方造成问题。
wrongOptions.D: 作者说的是禁止青少年使用的'世界'不现实，而非'没有社交媒体的世界难以想象'。

questions.questionText: What do we learn from the passage about British teenage girls?

options.label: A
options.text: The more frequently they interact on social media, the more they experience harassment.

options.label: B
options.text: The more time they spend on social media, the more likely they suffer from depression.

options.label: C
options.text: Most of them are engaged on social media for at least three hours a day.

options.label: D
options.text: They spend half as many hours on social media as British teenage boys.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第二段指出英国少女的高抑郁率'is closely correlated to time spent on social media'，即在社交媒体上花的时间越多越可能抑郁，与 B 一致。
questions.keySentence: the alarmingly high rate of depression in British teenage girls is closely correlated to time spent on social media

wrongOptions.A: 文中未建立'互动越频繁越易被骚扰'的因果关系。
wrongOptions.C: 原文是'two in five'（五分之二）而非大多数。
wrongOptions.D: 原文是男孩达到同等程度者数量为女孩一半，并非女孩上网时间是男孩一半。

questions.questionText: What is the author's view on the research finding about British teenage girls?

options.label: A
options.text: Its implications about online abuse are obvious.

options.label: B
options.text: Its key message calls for immediate attention.

options.label: C
options.text: Its importance should not be undervalued.

options.label: D
options.text: Its uncertainty should not go unnoticed.

questions.analysis: 观点态度题。第三段指出尽管研究未证明因果，但'the importance of the finding that there is a connection should not be underestimated'，与 C（其重要性不应被低估）几乎同义。
questions.keySentence: the importance of the finding that there is a connection should not be underestimated

wrongOptions.A: 作者未称其对网络欺凌的含义'显而易见'。
wrongOptions.B: 作者强调不可低估其重要性，而非'需立即关注'。
wrongOptions.D: 作者强调的是'重要性'不应低估，而非'不确定性'不应被忽视。

questions.questionText: What do experts think of health secretary Matt Hancock's idea?

options.label: A
options.text: Its implementation requires prompt action.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a welcome initiative but is long overdue.

options.label: C
options.text: Its success depends on how it is implemented.

options.label: D
options.text: It is too simplistic to produce the desired effect.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第四段说该想法优点在于'simplicity'，但'some experts question its effects'并呼吁更多区分，认为上网时间本身不坏、关键在于做什么，即专家认为它过于简单、难以奏效，与 D 一致。
questions.keySentence: some experts question its effects and call for a greater degree of differentiation

wrongOptions.B: 'long overdue'在原文指对数字巨头的法定监管，而非专家对 Hancock 想法的评价。
wrongOptions.C: 专家质疑其效果，而非说成败取决于如何实施。

questions.questionText: Besides social media companies, what factors contribute to young people's psychological health problems?

options.label: A
options.text: Poorly financed schools and health services.

options.label: B
options.text: Politicians' eagerness to divert public attention.

options.label: C
options.text: Bad statutory regulation of digital media giants.

options.label: D
options.text: Their parents' educational background and life.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。末段指出社交媒体公司并非万恶之源，年轻人抑郁上升还有其他原因，其中提到政客借此转移人们对'inadequately resourced schools and health services'的注意力，即资源不足的学校与医疗服务也是相关因素，与 A 一致。
questions.keySentence: politicians keen to divert attention from inadequately resourced schools and health services

wrongOptions.B: 政客转移注意力是其行为，而非导致心理问题的因素。
wrongOptions.C: '糟糕的法定监管'非原文所列致病因素。
wrongOptions.D: 文中未提及父母的教育背景与生活。

questionGroups.title: Passage 2

paragraphs.text: About a decade ago, the G-20, a forum of the world's biggest economies, agreed to crack down on multinational corporations' abusive use of tax havens. This resulted in a plan that aimed to curb practices that shielded a large chunk of corporate profits from tax authorities.
paragraphs.translation: 大约十年前，由世界最大经济体组成的论坛 G-20 同意打击跨国公司滥用避税天堂的行为。这促成了一项计划，旨在遏制那些使大量企业利润免于被税务机关征税的做法。

paragraphs.text: But, instead of reining in the use of tax havens—countries such as the Bahamas and Cayman Islands with very low or no effective tax rates—the problem has only gotten worse.
paragraphs.translation: 但结果并没有遏制住对避税天堂——如实际税率极低或为零的巴哈马和开曼群岛等国家——的利用，问题反而愈演愈烈。

paragraphs.text: In a new study, we measured the excessive profits reported in tax havens that cannot be explained by ordinary economic activity such as employees, factories and research in that country. Our findings show a striking pattern of artificial shifting of paper profits to tax havens by corporations, which has been relentless since the 1980s.
paragraphs.translation: 在一项新研究中，我们测算了在避税天堂申报的、无法用当地雇员、工厂和研究等正常经济活动来解释的超额利润。我们的研究结果显示出一种惊人的模式：企业人为地将账面利润转移到避税天堂，自20世纪80年代以来一直有增无减。

paragraphs.text: We found that the world's biggest multinational businesses shifted 37% of the profits— $969 billion—they earned in other countries to tax havens in 2019. The figure was less than 2% in the 1970s. The main reasons for the large increase were the growth of the tax avoidance industry in the 1980s and U.S. policies that made it easier to shift profits from high-tax countries to tax havens.
paragraphs.translation: 我们发现，2019年，世界最大的跨国企业将它们在其他国家赚取利润的37%——即9690亿美元——转移到了避税天堂。这一比例在20世纪70年代还不到2%。大幅增长的主要原因是20世纪80年代避税产业的兴起，以及美国出台的、使利润更容易从高税国家转移到避税天堂的政策。

paragraphs.text: We estimate that the amount of corporate taxes lost as a result reached 10% of total corporate revenue in 2019, up from less than 0.1% in the 1970s. In 2019, the total government tax loss globally was $250 billion. U.S. multinational corporations alone accounted for about half of that, followed by the U.K. and Germany.
paragraphs.translation: 我们估计，由此导致的企业税流失在2019年达到企业总收入的10%，而在20世纪70年代还不到0.1%。2019年，全球政府税收损失总额为2500亿美元。仅美国跨国公司就约占其中的一半，其次是英国和德国。

paragraphs.text: How do policymakers fix this? So far, the world as a whole has been trying to solve this problem by cutting or scrapping corporate taxes in a very gradual way. In the past 40 years, the global effective corporate tax rate has fallen from 23% to 17%. At the same time, governments have relied more heavily on consumption taxes.
paragraphs.translation: 政策制定者如何解决这一问题？到目前为止，整个世界一直试图以非常渐进的方式，通过削减或取消企业税来解决这一问题。在过去40年里，全球实际企业税率已从23%降至17%。与此同时，各国政府越来越依赖消费税。

paragraphs.text: But the root cause of profit-shifting is the incentives involved, such as generous or lenient corporate tax rates in other countries. If countries could agree on a global minimum corporate tax rate of, say, 20%, the problem of profit-shifting would largely disappear, as tax havens would simply cease to exist.
paragraphs.translation: 但利润转移的根本原因在于其中的激励因素，比如其他国家慷慨或宽松的企业税率。如果各国能够就一个全球最低企业税率——比如说20%——达成一致，利润转移问题将在很大程度上消失，因为避税天堂将不复存在。

paragraphs.text: This type of mechanism is exactly what more than 130 countries signed onto in 2021, with implementation of a 15% minimum tax set to begin soon in the EU, U.K., Japan, Indonesia and many other countries. The U.S. has notably not been able to pass this legislation.
paragraphs.translation: 正是这种机制，130多个国家在2021年签署加入，欧盟、英国、日本、印度尼西亚等许多国家即将开始实施15%的最低税率。值得注意的是，美国一直未能通过这项立法。

paragraphs.text: Our research suggests implementing this type of tax reform is necessary in reversing the shift of ever-greater amounts of corporate profits to tax havens—instead of being taxed by the governments where they operate and create value.
paragraphs.translation: 我们的研究表明，要扭转越来越多的企业利润流向避税天堂——而不是由其经营并创造价值所在国政府征税——的趋势，实施这类税制改革是必要的。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What do we learn about the G-20's agreement on curbing the use of tax havens?

options.label: A
options.text: It has aggravated the problem in non-G-20 countries.

options.label: B
options.text: It has taken a toll on countries such as Cayman Islands.

options.label: C
options.text: It has failed to achieve the expected outcome.

options.label: D
options.text: It has failed to result in any long-term plan.

questions.analysis: 细节推断题。第一、二段指出 G-20 曾同意打击避税天堂并制定了计划，但'instead of reining in the use of tax havens... the problem has only gotten worse'，说明协议未达到预期效果，与 C 一致。
questions.keySentence: instead of reining in the use of tax havens... the problem has only gotten worse.

wrongOptions.A: 文中未提及对非 G-20 国家加剧了问题。
wrongOptions.B: 并未说明该协议'重创'了开曼群岛等国。
wrongOptions.D: 第一段明确说协议促成了一项计划（a plan），故非'未产生任何长期计划'。

questions.questionText: What mainly accounted for the large increase in the world's biggest multinational corporations' shift of profits to tax havens?

options.label: A
options.text: Fluctuating tax rates globally.

options.label: B
options.text: Lenient policies of the U.S.

options.label: C
options.text: Heavy taxes imposed on them.

options.label: D
options.text: Rapid growth of their business.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第四段指出大幅增长的主要原因是80年代避税产业的兴起，以及'U.S. policies that made it easier to shift profits'，即美国的宽松政策，与 B 一致。
questions.keySentence: U.S. policies that made it easier to shift profits from high-tax countries to tax havens.

wrongOptions.A: '全球税率波动'非原文所述原因。
wrongOptions.C: 并未提及对它们征收重税导致转移。
wrongOptions.D: 增长指利润转移比例，而非其业务快速增长。

questions.questionText: What have policymakers been doing to prevent government tax loss?

options.label: A
options.text: Reducing corporate taxes step by step.

options.label: B
options.text: Scrapping consumption taxes gradually.

options.label: C
options.text: Making joint efforts to levy corporate taxes.

options.label: D
options.text: Adjusting global effective corporate tax rates.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第六段指出世界一直'by cutting or scrapping corporate taxes in a very gradual way'来试图解决问题，即逐步削减企业税，与 A 一致。
questions.keySentence: the world as a whole has been trying to solve this problem by cutting or scrapping corporate taxes in a very gradual way.

wrongOptions.B: 原文是各国更依赖消费税，而非逐步取消消费税。
wrongOptions.C: 并未提及'共同努力征收企业税'。
wrongOptions.D: 全球实际税率下降是结果描述，而非政策制定者采取的应对手段。

questions.questionText: What does the author say would bring tax havens to an end?

options.label: A
options.text: The alignment of corporate taxes with consumption taxes.

options.label: B
options.text: The implementation of generous tax rates in all countries.

options.label: C
options.text: The agreement on the root cause of global profit-shifting.

options.label: D
options.text: The imposition of a global minimum corporate tax rate.

questions.analysis: 细节理解题。第七段指出若各国能就'a global minimum corporate tax rate'达成一致，利润转移问题将基本消失，'as tax havens would simply cease to exist'，即全球最低企业税率会终结避税天堂，与 D 一致。
questions.keySentence: If countries could agree on a global minimum corporate tax rate... as tax havens would simply cease to exist.

wrongOptions.A: 并未提及使企业税与消费税'对齐'。
wrongOptions.B: 在所有国家实施'慷慨税率'恰恰是助长转移的诱因，与结论相反。
wrongOptions.C: 文中给出根本原因，但终结避税天堂靠的是最低税率，而非'就根源达成一致'。

questions.questionText: What could be expected of the global problem of profit-shifting in the near future?

options.label: A
options.text: It would be solved with more countries cutting tax rates.

options.label: B
options.text: It would end with governments' awareness of its severity.

options.label: C
options.text: It would cease to exist with worldwide corporate support.

options.label: D
options.text: It would continue because of noncooperation from the U.S.

questions.analysis: 推断题。第八段指出130多个国家已签署最低税率机制、即将实施，但'The U.S. has notably not been able to pass this legislation'，末段强调改革的必要性，暗示美国不合作会使利润转移问题继续存在，与 D 一致。
questions.keySentence: The U.S. has notably not been able to pass this legislation.

wrongOptions.A: 作者认为削减税率是渐进且无效的做法，并非解决之道。
wrongOptions.B: 仅意识到严重性并不能终结问题。
wrongOptions.C: 企业转移利润出于自身利益，'全球企业支持'不合逻辑。

questionGroups.sourceText: 科技进步使中国的医疗事业得到快速发展。近年来，远程医疗使优质医疗资源惠及更多患者。医学专家可以通过视频为偏远地区患者提供咨询，指导当地医生制定并实施治疗方案。人工智能辅助诊断系统帮助医生识别患者的早期症状，提高诊断准确率。电子健康档案的普及让医生能够快速了解患者病史，避免重复检查。线上医疗咨询平台极大地方便了患者就诊。科技与医疗的深度融合更好地满足了人民的健康需求。

answer.modelTranslation: Advances in technology have enabled China's medical sector to develop rapidly. In recent years, telemedicine has brought high-quality medical resources within reach of more patients. Medical experts can offer consultations to patients in remote areas via video and guide local doctors in formulating and implementing treatment plans. AI-assisted diagnostic systems help doctors identify patients' early symptoms and improve the accuracy of diagnosis. The widespread use of electronic health records allows doctors to quickly learn about a patient's medical history and avoid repeated examinations. Online medical consultation platforms have greatly facilitated patients' access to medical care. The deep integration of technology and healthcare has better met the health needs of the people.
